standard.title: Spelling: word origins, morphology and letter patterns
standard.description: use knowledge of known words, word origins including some Latin and Greek roots, base words, prefixes, suffixes, letter patterns and spelling generalisations to spell new words including technical words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can build and spell new words from knowledge of known words, base words, prefixes and suffixes (AC9E5LY09). They have not yet applied specific Latin and Greek root knowledge (beyond the most common), or used etymology systematically to access the spelling and meaning of technical words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use knowledge of word origins (including Latin and Greek roots), base words, prefixes, suffixes, letter patterns and spelling generalisations to spell new words including technical words.

nodes.label: Latin and Greek roots for spelling
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use knowledge of some Latin and Greek roots to spell and understand the meaning of words derived from those roots.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the root (Greek or Latin) in at least three provided words and explain how knowledge of the root helps with spelling and meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Use a dictionary to explore word origins; apply knowledge of Greek roots (e.g. 'ath' — outstanding skill, 'pent' — five, 'dec' — ten) to spell and understand words including technical vocabulary; explain how root knowledge helps decode and spell unfamiliar words.
wider: Research the meanings of five or more Greek or Latin roots and generate a family of words for each, explaining meaning connections
Investigate the meanings of words in languages of First Nations Australians using dictionaries or online resources from state libraries or universities
nodes.hinge_reason: Students without a working repertoire of root meanings cannot apply morphemic strategies to prefixes and suffixes in Node 2 — the prefix/suffix application presupposes that base word origins are recognisable.

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a repertoire of root meanings before the strategy of using etymology to spell and decode becomes productive. Building a small but well-understood set of roots is more effective than a superficial encounter with many.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Investigating First Nations Australian language word meanings through resources from state libraries or universities is both required by the elaborations and genuinely rich — it develops cultural understanding alongside vocabulary knowledge.
success_criteria: Identifies the Greek or Latin root in at least two provided words
Explains how knowing the root meaning helps with both spelling and word meaning

nodes.label: Prefixes, suffixes and meaning relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can expand knowledge of prefixes and suffixes and explore meaning relationships between words in the same morphemic family.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the prefix or suffix in at least three provided words and explain how each affix changes the word's meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Expand knowledge of prefixes and suffixes by exploring meaning relationships between words; use morphemic knowledge to spell and understand technical vocabulary (e.g. 'metaphorical', 'biology', 'biodegradable'); apply prefix and suffix knowledge to spell new words accurately.
wider: Build a morphemic word map showing a family of words sharing a root, prefix or suffix, showing meaning connections
Apply morphemic knowledge to spell technical vocabulary from curriculum-area learning (science, mathematics, history) and explain the morphemic components
success_criteria: Identifies at least one prefix or suffix and explains how it modifies the base word's meaning
Spells at least two words correctly using morphemic knowledge

nodes.label: Applying spelling generalisations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply accumulated knowledge of letter patterns and spelling generalisations to spell new words, including irregular and technically complex words.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly spell at least three provided words that require applying a spelling generalisation (e.g. doubling rules, y-to-i changes, -ible/-able patterns); identify the generalisation applied.
nodes.typical_width: Apply accumulated knowledge of a wide range of letter patterns and spelling generalisations to spell new words; use knowledge of common patterns to spell words including 'ratio', 'synthesis', 'reliability', 'handkerchief', 'receive', 'lollies', 'trolleys', 'climbing', 'designed', 'emergency'.
wider: Compare sets of words that seem to break a spelling rule and identify the underlying pattern that explains the 'exceptions'
Apply spelling generalisation knowledge to read and write technical words encountered in curriculum-area texts, explaining the generalisation used

response_modes.reason: Spelling accuracy requires overlearning — students who know the generalisation still need repeated encounter with its application in diverse words before accurate spelling becomes automatic. Targeted practice with words that consistently cause errors is the productive investment here.

success_criteria: Correctly spells at least three provided words requiring application of a spelling generalisation
Names the generalisation applied in at least one case
